exactGap: A durable per-member, per-room read marker exists (spaceReadMarkers.ts) and the open room derives unread threads from it, but the sidebar unread and working dots come from a browser-only store that holds only rooms whose page has published and is cleared when the reader leaves the room (space-live-work.ts, SpacePage.tsx:173-175), so there is no server-side cross-room aggregate, mark-all-read, mention count or needs-you count. Room-scoped pieces already exist that the item should extend: the Activity panel's 'Needs attention' lens over salience-ranked items, a cross-room agent registry (/agents/installations and /agents/chief-core, presence only, no run or needs-you state) and a generic notification feed API (list, unread count, mark-all-read) that only chat surfaces read. No Home or needs-you inbox, snooze/dismiss, mention/thread slices or cross-room Activity view exists; the sidebar 'Home' group is the dashboard and the support inbox owns the /inbox route.
reuse: spaceReadMarkers table and the pure unreadThreadIds/advanceMarker derivation (per-member state already lives in the Application Plane)
Control's Space index (GET internal/spaces for the verified subject, listSpacesForSubject) as the single visibility filter for any cross-room aggregate
SpaceActivityItem, salience ordering (orderActivity) and the 'attention' lens in SpaceActivityPanel as the item renderer for a needs-you slice
getAgentInstallations registry (ADR-0002), AgentInstallationsPage and chief-core routing as the cross-room Agents destination
notification-core feed API (list, unread count, mark-all-read) for non-ZDR out-of-app signals
spacePresence heartbeat table (30 s window) for sidebar presence once an aggregate exists
constraints: Space access never widens an owner-plane ACL: the aggregate must be metadata-only and filtered by Control's Space index so no title, count or activity leaks for a room the viewer cannot read, and inbox items stay refs-only and are rehydrated at render under the viewer's current decision. Per-room thread reads need a Control read decision per Space per call (spaces.rs:1268-1330), so a cross-room read cannot loop over rooms with those decisions. notification-core is not a ZDR-safe store: a ZDR request persists no payload and is never projected into the feed (service.go:337, :522; feed_projection.go:133), so an inbox backed by that feed would silently drop ZDR orgs. Push for external devices needs the Channel Plane, which is docs-only.
approachAdjustment: Back the Home inbox with an Application-Plane attention projection of refs only (Convex, next to spaceReadMarkers), or state explicitly that refs-only signals are standard retention under ZDR, and use notification-core only for out-of-app delivery. Phase it: first a polled GET /api/v1/spaces/attention (Control Space index intersected with read markers and a new Session Core per-Space latest-activity summary) to drive sidebar counts and mark-all-read, then the Home inbox, then stream push through F-t1-003. Extend /agents/installations and chief-core with run and needs-you state instead of building a second Agents destination. Name the destination carefully because 'Home' is the dashboard and /inbox is the support inbox.
effortNote: L stands if the stream transport stays in F-t1-003; the Model Plane per-Space summary read, a ZDR-safe attention store and the inbox UI make it a multi-plane L, while the polled first slice alone is about M.
verdictReason: The cross-room aggregate and inbox are genuinely absent, but the item understates what exists (durable read marker, room Needs-attention lens, cross-room agent registry, notification feed API) and its notification-core-style store cannot hold ZDR data.

exactGap: There is no room-level push: SpacePage polls the thread projection every 6 s while the tab is visible (SpacePage.tsx:87,298), the gateway has no Space stream route (spaces.rs router 649-738), Convex has no per-Space event table or seq (only lifecycle, audience, deletion and presence tables), and Session Core's outbox may publish only audit and mp.v1.run.<id>.event subjects (audit_publisher.rs:69), so no thread-appended event exists to project. Reusable plumbing does exist: Last-Event-ID resume for the sender's own run stream (chat/streams.rs:134-200), Convex leased outbox rows (schema.ts:680-717), Control's Space-scoped read decision carrying the audience revision (shared_thread_read_decision.go), a gateway JetStream consumer precedent (gdpr_nats.rs) and an org-wide run-lifecycle mirror (nats.ts:996-1030) that drops space and thread ids.

Convex leased-outbox pattern (spaceLifecycleEvents, spaceRecipientAudienceEvents: claim, lease, ack, retry)

Gateway async-nats JetStream consumer precedent (gdpr_nats.rs) and the Redis/Dragonfly connection already used by the rate limiter
The existing 6 s visible-tab poll as the degraded fallback
constraints: Space access never widens an owner-plane ACL: frames carry ids and kinds only and every delivery is re-checked against a live Control decision, but those decisions are action- and audience-pinned and expire after 2 minutes (personal_thread_decision.go:21), and the audience set is closed to Session Core and sandbox-manager (shared_thread_read_decision.go:44-50), so a stream needs a new Control audience rather than reusing the Session Core read token. ZDR must propagate: frames and replay buffers stay content-free, and the BFF already holds a Dragonfly copy of chat content that erasure had to reach (gdpr_nats.rs:1-30), so do not add bodies to this path. Session Core owns thread content and shared-bus NATS is plain, best-effort (space_membership_nats.rs:1-30), so any projection must be rebuildable from a snapshot. The Application and Ingestion NATS mirrors are disabled pending a scoped principal and the Model Plane mirror is optional (nats-subscriber.js:288, 324-327).
approachAdjustment: Do not make the Application Plane the first emitter of room events: posts and runs happen in Session Core, so add a thread/message event subject family to Session Core's outbox (extend classify_outbox_subject and the publisher ACLs) and consume it in the gateway or an Application projection; evaluate Session Core's own events journal as the sequence source before adding a Convex seq table. Slice it: run-state frames first over the existing mp.v1.run.*.event path (the envelope must carry space_id and thread_id, which the Convex mirror currently drops), then post frames. Add the stream-read audience to Control's closed set and re-authorize on every heartbeat, and keep the poll as degraded mode.
effortNote: Unchanged: it spans Session Core outbox and NATS ACLs, an Application projection, a Control audience, a gateway SSE endpoint with NATS or Redis fan-out and the SPA store.
verdictReason: The recommendation is correct and the substrate is absent in code (polling only), but the item puts the first event emitter in the Application Plane when Session Core is the only plane that sees a post or run state change.

exactGap: Only run-completion notifications exist: capability-core may send modelplane.run_completed and modelplane.run_failed to users who registered a per-run watcher (notification-core handlers.go:199-215, runwatch/consumer.go:64-91), and the watcher button is wired in Chat, not in Space rooms. mention.received exists only as a seeded preference row (migration 005:60-62) with no producer, @person mentions are plain composer text (SpaceRoomComposer.tsx:196-210, 297-303), and the gateway may notify only the delegated user itself (handlers.go:160-168). There is no Space deep-link contract, signal taxonomy, per-room level, hide-preview flag or Space thread follow/mute, although the support inbox has conversation follow plus a refs-only JetStream notification consumer that are patterns to copy.
evidence: apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/chat/components/ChatMessages.tsx:3685 (grep hit: RunNotifyButton is used in Chat only)
reuse: notification-core Accept path, per-user per-event preference rows and feed API

spaceReadMarkers (per-member Convex state) as the home for per-room levels and thread subscriptions

constraints: Space posts and runs live in Session Core, not conversation-core (conversation-core is the support-inbox conversation owner, space_activity.go:35-54), so mention and reply records must originate where the message is owned or in an Application projection fed from it. The delegated gateway principal can notify only the signed-in user (handlers.go:160-168), so notifying another person needs a service producer with a per-type allowlist. notification-core under ZDR persists no payload, refuses async queueing and never projects to the in-app feed (service.go:296-345, :522; feed_projection.go:133), so 'refs-only payload plus hide-preview on for ZDR orgs' does not yield in-app signals for ZDR orgs until a policy decision is made; also Space ZDR (effect policy) and org interactive ZDR are different flags. Recipients must be re-authorized at render (Space access never widens an owner-plane ACL), and push or chat-app delivery depends on the docs-only Channel Plane.
approachAdjustment: Replace 'conversation-core persists a mention record on post' with: send structured person mentions on the post wire (the composer sends only mentionedAgentRef today), record them with the message owner (Session Core metadata or an Application spaceMentions projection) and publish metadata-only events that a notification-core JetStream consumer turns into notifications, copying conversation_followed_message.go. Extend capability-core's allowlist for agent_done, agent_awaiting and approval_needed, and auto-register run watchers for runs a person starts in a room instead of the manual per-run toggle. Decide the ZDR delivery rule before building the preview flag. Keep per-room levels and follow/mute as a second slice.
effortNote: Raised from L: signals originate in three planes, structured mentions do not exist on the wire, and in-app delivery under ZDR needs a new rule; slice one (taxonomy, allowlist, mention/approval/agent_done producers, deep link) is L and per-room levels plus follow/mute add M.
verdictReason: The gap is real, but the approach names the wrong owner for Space mention records and assumes a refs-only payload survives ZDR in notification-core; it also omits that run-completion notification and support-inbox follow already exist as reusable patterns.

exactGap: The only SCIM code is a fake-success intake in the Ingestion Plane: /api/v1/scim/v2/* authenticates a per-org bearer token, stores a webhook event, publishes scim_event_received and answers 201, 204 or an empty list without creating or changing anyone (integration-corev2 server.go:1237-1275, 2758-2790), and no Control Plane service consumes the event or implements Users or Groups. SSO is the better-auth plugin enabled only by the global SSO_ENABLED flag with no per-org enforcement or verification flow wired, and Settings honestly shows 'not configured' (auth.ts:1019-1030, WorkspaceSettingsPage.tsx:1238-1250). Unconnected substrate exists in Control: sso_provider rows with organization_id and domain, org-core organization_domains (pending|verified|revoked, auto_invite flag, one verified owner per domain) with no verification handler, org_tenant_links, a 'suspended' member status, and session-revoke APIs.
evidence: apps/Control Plane/auth-core/src/grpc/auth/v1/auth.ts:188-200 (grep hit: RevokeSession and RevokeAllSessions contracts)
reuse: org-core organization_domains table, DomainInvitationEligible policy and the one-verified-owner unique index for domain verification and allowlist or auto-join
better-auth sso_provider (organization_id, domain, oidc/saml config) behind the existing sso() plugin and organizationProvisioning hooks
org-core OrgMember.status 'suspended' and OrgTenantLink for Microsoft tenant resolution
auth-core RevokeSession and RevokeAllSessions plus the membership_changed to Session Core revocation chain
integration-corev2 scim_tokens store (hashed per-org bearer tokens, audited create and revoke) as a model to re-home
constraints: Identity lifecycle is Control-owned, but the SCIM endpoint sits in the Ingestion Plane, so an Ingestion-published event must not drive org membership; re-home the endpoint and token store to org-core rather than bridging over NATS. Space access already requires an active org membership at Control (repository.go:828-852), so flipping a member to suspended or removed cuts new Space decisions at once; the remaining gaps are in-flight runs (revocation events ride plain NATS), the organization room's roster rows (never re-synced, see F-t1-022) and agent owner links, which Control does not hold (agents.createdBy is optional and Convex-side). Enforcing SSO needs a break-glass owner, domain verification must be real because the org-core table itself says a Brreg match is not proof, and external-identity principal links wait for the docs-only Channel Plane.
approachAdjustment: Lead with the one-line safety fix: make the integration-corev2 SCIM data routes refuse (501) so no IdP believes a deprovision succeeded. Then build on organization_domains (add the DNS or IdP verification flow, an enforce-SSO flag and a break-glass owner there) and the sso_provider organization and domain columns instead of new per-org stores, and implement SCIM Users in org-core mapping deactivate to member status suspended. Treat the suspend-the-person's-agents cascade as dependent on an agent-owner link in Control (F-t1-043), and leave Groups and principal links for later slices.
effortNote: Raised from L as one item: the 501 fix is S, per-org SSO with domain verification is M, SCIM Users is L, Groups and agent suspension add L; recommend splitting.
verdictReason: SCIM is a fake-success stub in the wrong plane and SSO is flag-only, so the gap is real, but the item misses the existing org-core domain, tenant-link and suspended-status substrate and should lead with the S-sized refusal fix.

exactGap: Room agents exist end to end (create-in-room, bind an org agent, pause/resume/revoke, agents held in Control as service subjects), and a binding already stores and the gateway already enforces triggerModes, allowedTools and approvalMode (schema.ts:606-678, spaces.rs apply_mention_binding_policy), but no route or dialog edits them and model, language, proactivity and thread policy are deliberately not stored. Personal agents, a primary-agent setting, an agent owner access list and add policy, and a private assistant beside the room are absent: the agents table has only an optional createdBy, listInstallableSpaceAgentsForGateway returns every org definition to any room owner or manager, and Control accepts Application's declared service roster with no per-agent policy check. A personal Space is single-subject by construction and ReplaceMemberships refuses it, so 'bring my agent' cannot be done by widening that roster.

constraints: Space access never widens an owner-plane ACL: a personal agent in a shared room may use only what the room's audience may see, and owner connected-account tools still need owner-plane grants. A personal Space stays single-subject (repository.go:669-675), so a personal agent must be an owner-derived subject rather than a roster widening. No org-approved model list has an owner today (allowed_models is refused as homeless, grpc.rs:150-160; only a process-wide ALLOWED_MODELS env exists, normalize.rs:86-100), so 'model from the org-approved list' needs a Control-owned list first.

First expose the existing binding policy (trigger mode, tools, approval) through a PATCH route and a settings dialog, and add model and language only once the org-approved model list has an owner (shared with F-t1-006). Second, make the agent access list and add policy Control authority enforced at the roster-replace boundary or a new bind decision, because Control performs no per-agent check today; filter the installable list by the caller's add right. Third, personal agents and the private panel, which also depend on an agent-owner link, audience-safe disclosure (F-t1-012) and addressing (F-t1-002). Do not describe room-agent configuration as wholly absent.
effortNote: Raised from L as one item: slice one is S to M, the Control access list and add policy is M to L, and personal agents with the private panel is XL.
verdictReason: Personal agents, the access list and the private panel are absent, but binding-level trigger, tool and approval policy already exists and is enforced, so the item must not call room-agent configuration missing; it also places the add-policy check in a Control path that does not exist yet.

exactGap: Control already stores and converges viewer|editor|manager|owner roles with an owner guard (repository.go:646-733), but Application can only grant 'editor' (spaceMemberGrants.role is a literal, schema.ts:831, spaceMembers.ts:85), the gateway has only POST /members and DELETE /members/{id} (spaces.rs:677-682) and SpaceMemberControls has no role control. The Convex spaces row has a name but no topic, its lifecycle union and Control registration_state have no archived value, and room deletion is not authorized (the deletion policy admits personal Spaces only), so rename, topic, archive and restore do not exist. syncAllOrganizationRooms has no caller and convex-core has no crons file, so the organization room's roster is declared once at activation (spaces.ts:1441) and never re-synced even though a durable org member_changed consumer already runs (nats-subscriber.js:305-316, nats.ts:221).
reuse: Control ReplaceMemberships (honors a declared role per subject, never revokes the owner by absence, advances revisions only on real change)
spaceMemberGrants, roomMembersForControl and the gateway sync_room_members declaration path
syncOrganizationRoom, syncAllOrganizationRooms and listActiveOrganizationRooms, plus the durable member_changed consumer (nats:onOrganizationMembershipProjectionChanged) as the event hook
Application lifecycle transition and outbox machinery (transitionLifecycle, spaceLifecycleEvents) for an archived state
SpaceMemberControls and the gateway's room-role gate (require_space_agent_grant_role) as the UI and authorization shell
constraints: Control owns membership and role; Application's list is intent only, and the replace-memberships request carries no acting subject (MembershipReplacement has only space_ref, members and managed types), so rank rules such as canGrant and last-owner cannot be enforced at Control through the current declarative PUT; use a per-member grant or change-role endpoint that carries the acting subject, or add the actor to the contract. A demotion advances membership and authority revisions only on a real change, which is what invalidates in-flight signed decisions. Archive must be a Control registration_state that denies writes and allows reads, not a UI flag, and room delete with a restore window needs the retention and deletion saga, which authorizes personal Spaces only and must honor legal hold and ZDR immediate purge. The organization room's roster stays derived from org-core (everyone maps to editor), so role editing must exclude it. Control already requires an active org membership at resolution time (repository.go:828-852), so removed members lose access live and the roster sync gap is mostly that new members never appear.
approachAdjustment: Split the bundle. The genuine quick wins are the organization-room reconcile (a convex crons file calling syncAllOrganizationRooms plus a hook in the existing member_changed handler) and rename or topic. Role change and archive need Control contract changes (per-member endpoint with the acting subject, an archived registration_state with decision gating) and are M to L. Drop 'delete with a restore window' from this item until the deletion saga covers shared rooms.
effortNote: Raised from M: role change and archive each touch Control's contract and state machine; only the reconcile and rename or topic remain quick wins (S each).
verdictReason: Every claim checks out against code, but the item bundles two true quick wins with Control-contract changes and a deletion dependency, and its quickWin label and M estimate should apply only to the reconcile and rename or topic slices.

exactGap: Control stores one deny-by-default space_effect_policies row per org holding privacy attestations and entitlement booleans (EffectPolicy, migrations 018-028), but its only writer is a service-principal PUT (server.go:354, spaces.go:98-106, service_auth.go:134) used through an operator script (scripts/set-space-effect-policy.sh); the gateway and SPA have no admin route or UI, and Control denials are plain-string 403 or 503 bodies with no reason code (writeSpaceEvidenceError, spaces.go:1455-1465). Per-binding agent policy (triggerModes, allowedTools, approvalMode) is stored and enforced in the gateway, a per-run AutonomyRung ladder is enforced per call in execution-core but granted only by a human-approved plan, and capability rollout states (stable, canary, quarantine, deprecated) exist. Absent: org-level posting rules, an agent or model allowlist (allowed_models is refused as having no owner), an org-set autonomy posture, per-principal-kind rate limits (rate_limit.rs keys by org, user or IP) and org feature flags with rings and overrides (billing-core has only plan-level boolean maps).
reuse: The EffectPolicy fields and the set-space-effect-policy.sh validation as the contract for an admin editor
Gateway orgs domain (require_org_admin, org settings routes) and WorkspaceSettingsPage sections, which already host the org ZDR and quota admin controls
Binding policy (triggerModes, allowedTools, approvalMode) and apply_mention_binding_policy for per-room posting and tool rules
AutonomyRung and check_autonomy_rung (enforced per call) as the ceiling for an autonomy posture
capability-core rollout_state (quarantine and deprecated) as the kill-switch precedent, and billing-core entitlements for plan caps
Control audit-core events for every policy change
constraints: The effect policy is Control's processing and entitlement floor, written only by a dedicated Control workload; its privacy fields (purpose, lawful basis, privacy class, retention class, residency, deletion scope, zero_data_retention) are compliance attestations that the provisioning script says must never be defaulted (set-space-effect-policy.sh:14-19), so presets and an org-admin editor must not overwrite them, and a missing row must stay a denial. Entitlements are floors that never authorize an owner-plane resource, so the admin surface cannot widen any owner-plane ACL. Space ZDR in this row is a separate flag from the org-core interactive ZDR toggle already in Settings, so the UI must show and reconcile both (DOC, design-zdr.json). The gateway cannot call the writer (policy principal only), so the admin route must be a new gateway-delegated, org-admin-checked Control endpoint. Flags are rollout controls only, never authorization.
approachAdjustment: Phase 1 should expose only the entitlement booleans (privacy attestation shown read-only), through a new org-admin-delegated Control route that validates against plan entitlements and emits audit events, and keep the service-only PUT for compliance fields; 'safe presets' must be presets of entitlements, not of privacy fields. Add a reason-code to Control's decision denials before building typed denial UI, because today the thread-read decline is swallowed as 'no shared read' (spaces.rs:1319). Do not present an org model allowlist as a toggle: allowed_models has no owning service and needs one first. Move posting rules, the agent and model allowlist, autonomy posture and flags into separate later items.
effortNote: Raised from L as one item: phase 1 alone is L (new Control route, typed denial codes across the Space decision endpoints, admin UI), and phases 2 and 3 add an owner for model allowlists, human-first posting rules, a posture and a flag registry.
verdictReason: The gap is real and phase 1 is the right priority, but 'safe presets' over the whole policy row would overwrite compliance attestations, typed denials need a Control change first, and the allowlist half has no owning service yet.

exactGap: No DM or group-DM path exists: Space kinds are personal|room|project|case in Control's CHECK constraint and validators and in Convex's kind union, and the gateway create route refuses everything except personal and room (spaces.rs:2873-2880); a personal Space is single-subject and cannot hold other members or an agent. The right primitives are present (an audience-revision ceiling on thread and run reads, run_service_grpc.rs:711-718, and non-personal kinds already take the shared decision path), but there is no participant_hash, per-viewer hide, DM sidebar section or adder-chosen history window. Human-to-human conversation is also not possible in today's posting model: every post is a model turn through streamChat, and Session Core's append_message and start_run require the thread's own owner, so a second participant cannot post into the first's thread.
reuse: Control registered_spaces and space_memberships with the existing shared decision path (kinds other than personal already resolve as shared)
The recipient-audience registration outbox and the audience-revision ceiling in Session Core's thread and run reads for the history window
Space thread-append decision (user-core) as the authority to carry into a non-owner append
Presence, typing and read-marker paths, which are keyed by Space and subject and need no change
The isOrganizationRoom explicit-flag precedent if a flag is preferred over a new kind
constraints: Space access never widens an owner-plane ACL, so a DM must be a Control-registered Space with a fixed roster and the same decision path. 'DM with my agent' must not be a dm Space containing an agent subject: a personal Space stays single-subject (Control refuses to replace its membership, repository.go:669-675), so that case is the personal scope plus an owner-derived personal agent (F-t1-011). History windows must be enforced where content is read (Session Core list filter and retrieval), not in the UI. Space deletion authorization covers personal Spaces only (deletion_authorization.go:17-22), so hide-versus-delete semantics for DMs are undefined.
approachAdjustment: Keep the dm and group_dm kind approach, whose plumbing is small (CHECK, two Control validators, Convex union, create route), but sequence it behind human-first, non-owner posting (F-t1-001): Session Core must accept a Control append decision from a non-owner member, because append_message and start_run currently demand OwnerIntent::Mutate, i.e. the thread owner. Correct the evidence pointer: the audience-revision read filter is run_service_grpc.rs:711-718, while grpc.rs:5340-5360 is the agent-skills listing. Model human-with-own-agent as the personal scope rather than as a dm Space with an agent member.
effortNote: L holds only if F-t1-001 carries the Session Core non-owner append work and the sidebar DM section; otherwise this is XL.
verdictReason: The gap is real and correctly absent in code, the approach fits Space authority, and only the posting dependency and one mis-cited evidence line need correcting.
